thread.title: UnitedHealthcare offers up (nearly) free Apple Watch devices as part of wellness program

author: Katharine Grayson
title: UnitedHealthcare offers up (nearly) free Apple Watch devices as part of wellness program
text: – Senior Reporter, Minneapolis / St. Paul Business Journal Nov 15, 2018, 6:30am EST A UnitedHealthcare corporate-wellness program will now reward participants who take enough steps daily with a nearly-free Apple Watch, the health insurance giant says. Employees enrolled in the insurer's Motion program must initially pay shipping fees and taxes for the watch, but will get to keep it if they walk 10,000 steps daily. Participants will earn $4 each day they meet activity requirements if they choose the insurer's "Walk it Off" option. That money can go toward the purchase price of the watch, allowing users to earn the device in about six months. Enrollees can get up to a Series 3 version of the device , CNBC reported. The price for Series 3 watches starts at about $279, according to Apple Inc.'s (Nasdaq: AAPL) website. UnitedHealthcare integrated the Apple Watch devices into its Motion program earlier this year. However, it didn’t reward participants with a nearly-free gadget at the time. UnitedHealthcare started incorporating wearables into its employer-wellness offerings in 2016. It has gone on to bring devices made by multiple manufacturers into the program. Several insurers and independent corporate-wellness companies have likewise incorporated wearable devices into their programs, allowing workers to earn incentives like gift cards in exchange for remaining active. (Early on, some people attempted to cheat the programs by slapping fitness trackers on their pets .) UnitedHealthcare has found that 56 percent of people who registered a wearable through the Motion program were active for at least six months, compared to about 29 percent for a gym membership, the company said in a statement. The company is now testing whether employees' use of wearables can reduce health care costs through a study of its own workforce, CNBC reported. UnitedHealthcare is the insurance arm of Minnetonka-based UnitedHealth Group Inc. (NYSE: UNH), which is Minnesota's largest public company. The company employs 2,861 people in the Triad, most out of its Greensboro office at 3603 N. Elm St. – Senior Reporter, Minneapolis / St. Paul Business Journal Nov 15, 2018, 6:30am EST Related Content
